title: Repair the bounds check
hints: Follow the three steps. Step 1 is done for you: the offset's bounds arrive as `lo` and `hi`. Steps 2 and 3 each have one mistake.
Step 2: a view of `k` elements that starts at `s` ends at element `s + k - 1`, and that must be at most `n - 1`. So the last allowed start is `n - k`, not `n - 1`.
Step 3 needs both ends: the smallest offset must be at least 0 and the largest must be at most `last_start`. Add the `lo` check next to the `hi` check.

answer.explain: The last allowed start is `n - k`, because a window of `k` elements starting there ends exactly at element `n - 1`. The view is proven when the whole range of the offset fits: `lo >= 0` and `hi <= n - k`. That is the spec's rule `lo >= 0` and `hi + k <= n` with `k` moved to the other side. When `k` is larger than `n`, `n - k` is negative, so nothing passes.
